summary: A cabin moved from Yager Butte in 1958 and rebuilt as an R-6 flat cab on Diamond Butte in 1970, staffed until 2001 and now an off-season Forest Service rental.

facts.design: R-6 flat cab on a 10-foot concrete base

access.note: Reachable by car plus a short, steep 200-foot walk; rented through Recreation.gov, off-season only

visit.trail_note: 200-foot walk up a steep hill from the parking area

facts.agency: Custer Gallatin National Forest / Bureau of Land Management

events.note: Cabin moved from Yager (Yeager) Butte to the current site
Present R-6 flat cab on 10-ft concrete base built
Active fire lookout use until 2001 per Recreation.gov
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register, April 12, 2022, as US 1529

evidence.supports: cabin moved from Yager Butte in 1958, R-6 flat cab on 10-ft concrete base built 1970
evidence.quote: Established with a cabin moved from Yager Butte in 1958, this R-6 flat cab atop a 10' concrete base, built in 1970, is available as an off-season rental.

evidence.supports: moved from Yeager Butte in 1958, active lookout until 2001
evidence.quote: The lookout was moved from its original location of Yeager Butte in 1958 and was an active fire lookout until 2001.

evidence.supports: elevation and view toward Bighorn Mountains, sagebrush terrain
evidence.quote: The lookout offers expansive views of the nearby hills and the distant Bighorn Mountains, which are about 100 miles away. Vegetation is sparse, but sagebrush and lupin thrive on the surrounding landscape.

evidence.supports: 200-foot walk from parking area to lookout
evidence.quote: The lookout is accessible by car, but it is a 200-foot walk up a steep hill to the lookout from the parking area.

evidence.supports: rental program, sleeps 4, propane appliances, wagon stored for hauling gear
evidence.quote: The lookout can accommodate 4 people and is furnished with a table, chairs and1 twin bed with mattress, a double futon with mattress and a cot. Propane appliances include a cook stove with an oven, lights and a heater. A few cooking and eating utensils are provided... A wagon is stored in the lookout's basement to help haul gear.

notes_for_editor: No source gives an original construction/first-staffed date before the 1958 relocation, or details on specific notable fires fought from this lookout. 'Yager' vs 'Yeager' Butte spelling differs between NHLR and Recreation.gov; story uses both forms once. firelookout.com (source 3) duplicates NHLR's text nearly verbatim, so it was used only to corroborate, not as an independent source.
